title: RRB NTPC CBT-2 — Mock Test 5
description: Full-length 100-question mock simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. 60 minutes total, no sectional timing, 2 marks/Q, -0.5 negative. Includes 5 inline Current-Affairs questions in the GA section (C2S Programme, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Retail inflation 1.7%, RELIEF scheme, Arjuna Award 2026) — refreshable from the admin CA pool.

questions.stem: Find the missing term: BD, FH, JL, NP, ?
questions.explanation: First letters: B(+4)→F→J→N→R. Second letters: D(+4)→H→L→P→T. Next pair = RT.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the missing term: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ?
questions.explanation: Squares of consecutive natural numbers: 1²=1, 2²=4, 3²=9, 4²=16, 5²=25, 6²=36.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the missing term: 7, 14, 28, 56, 112, ?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 'CAT' is coded as '24-26-7' (mirror cipher), how is 'DOG' coded?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'BOOK' is written as 'CPPL' (each letter +1). How is 'NEWS' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: N→O, E→F, W→X, S→T. So NEWS → OFXT.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a man, Suresh said, 'His son is the only brother of my mother.' How is the man related to Suresh?
questions.explanation: The only brother of Suresh's mother = Suresh's maternal uncle. The man's son is Suresh's maternal uncle, so the man is the FATHER of Suresh's maternal uncle, i.e. Suresh's maternal grandfather.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A's father is the only son of B's grandfather, then how is A related to B?
questions.explanation: B's grandfather has only one son = A's father = B's father. So A and B share the same father — they are siblings.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A man walks 6 km East, turns south and walks 8 km. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: 6-8-10 right triangle: distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: From a point, A walks 5 km East, then 4 km North, then 3 km West, then 2 km South. How far is A from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net East = 5 − 3 = 2 km. Net North = 4 − 2 = 2 km. Distance = √(2² + 2²) = √8 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All birds are animals. No animal is a fish.

Conclusions:
I. No bird is a fish.
II. Some animals are birds.
questions.explanation: I: All birds ⊂ animals; no animals are fish → no birds are fish. TRUE. II: All birds are animals → some animals are birds (since birds exist). TRUE. Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some pens are pencils. All pencils are erasers.

Conclusions:
I. Some pens are erasers.
II. All erasers are pencils.
questions.explanation: I: Some pens ⊂ pencils ⊂ erasers ⟹ some pens are erasers. TRUE. II: 'All pencils are erasers' does NOT imply 'all erasers are pencils'. FALSE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If P > Q ≥ R, R = S, and S > T, which of the following is NECESSARILY TRUE?
questions.explanation: P > Q ≥ R = S > T ⟹ P > T. TRUE. Other options either false or not necessarily true.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five boys A, B, C, D, E sit in a row. C is to the left of D and right of B. A is to the right of D. E is to the left of B. Who is at the extreme left?
questions.explanation: Order from left: E, B, C, D, A. E is at the extreme left.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 1 March 2024 was a Friday, what day was 1 March 2025?
questions.explanation: Between 1 March 2024 and 1 March 2025 = 365 days (Feb 2024 was 29 days but already past on 1 March). 365 mod 7 = 1 odd day. Friday + 1 = Saturday.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: How many times do the hour and minute hands of a clock coincide in 24 hours?
questions.explanation: In 12 hours, the hands coincide 11 times. In 24 hours, they coincide 22 times.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have exactly TWO faces painted?
questions.explanation: Cubes with 2 painted faces lie on edges (excluding corners). Number = 12(n−2) = 12 × 3 = 36.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Find the missing number:

2 | 3 | 4
5 | 7 | ?
10 | 21 | 36
questions.explanation: Pattern (per column): top × middle = bottom. Col 1: 2 × 5 = 10 ✓. Col 2: 3 × 7 = 21 ✓. Col 3: 4 × ? = 36 ⟹ ? = 9.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the odd one out:
questions.explanation: 64=4³, 125=5³, 216=6³ — all perfect cubes. 243 = 3⁵, not a cube. Odd: 243.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: BOOK : LIBRARY :: TREE : ?
questions.explanation: A library is a collection of books; a forest is a collection of trees.
questions.subject: REASONING

If '×' means '+' and '+' means '−', evaluate:

12 × 6 + 4
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Question: Who among A, B, C, D is the tallest?

Statement I: A is taller than B but shorter than C.
Statement II: D is taller than A but shorter than C.
questions.explanation: From I alone: B < A < C. C might be the tallest, but we don't know about D. From II alone: A < D < C. C might be the tallest, but we don't know about B. Combined: B < A < D < C. So C is definitely the tallest. Both together sufficient.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Choose the figure that comes next: △, ▽, △, ▽, △, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern alternates: △, ▽, △, ▽, △, so next is ▽.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Position from right = Total − Position from left + 1 = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29th.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Six friends — P, Q, R, S, T, U — are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. P is between U and S. Q is opposite to P. R is to the immediate right of Q. Who is to the immediate left of T?
questions.explanation: Going clockwise: P-S-?-Q-R-?-back to P. P between U & S means U-P-S clockwise. Q opposite P ⟹ at position 4. R to right of Q ⟹ R is clockwise of Q. So clockwise order: P, S, T, Q, R, U, P. Hence T's left = R.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for 'Right to Constitutional Remedies'?
questions.explanation: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies — Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it 'the heart and soul of the Constitution'.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64).

questions.stem: How many Fundamental Duties are listed in the Indian Constitution after the 86th Amendment (2002)?
questions.explanation: Originally 10 Fundamental Duties (42nd Amendment, 1976). The 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th — providing education to children aged 6-14.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a 'writ' issued by the Supreme Court under Article 32?

questions.stem: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is appointed by:

questions.stem: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between:
options: British East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah

questions.stem: The 'Quit India Movement' was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the AICC. Gandhi's famous slogan: 'Do or Die'.

questions.stem: Who founded the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1885?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, a retired British civil servant. W.C. Bonnerjee was its first president.

questions.stem: The 'Roof of the World' refers to which mountain range?

questions.stem: Which is the longest river in India?

questions.stem: The Strait of Malacca connects which two seas?

Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea

questions.stem: The chemical symbol of Gold is:
questions.explanation: Gold's chemical symbol is Au (from the Latin 'aurum'). Ag is Silver.

questions.stem: Which gland in the human body is known as the 'Master Gland'?

questions.explanation: Wind energy is renewable — it is naturally replenished. Coal, petroleum, and natural gas are fossil fuels (non-renewable).

questions.stem: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) established?

questions.stem: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?

questions.stem: Kuchipudi is a classical dance form of which Indian state?

questions.stem: A and B can complete a work in 18 and 24 days respectively. They worked together for 6 days, then A left. In how many days will B finish the remaining work alone?
questions.explanation: A's rate = 1/18, B's rate = 1/24. Combined rate = 1/18 + 1/24 = (4+3)/72 = 7/72. In 6 days, work done = 42/72 = 7/12. Remaining = 5/12. B's rate = 1/24, so days = (5/12)/(1/24) = 5/12 × 24 = 10 days.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths 200 m and 300 m run in opposite directions at speeds 50 km/h and 40 km/h. Find the time taken to cross each other.
questions.explanation: Relative speed = (50 + 40) km/h = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance = 500 m. Time = 500/25 = 20 sec.

questions.stem: The average weight of 5 boys is 50 kg. If one boy weighing 45 kg is replaced by a new boy, the average becomes 52 kg. Find the new boy's weight.
questions.explanation: Original sum = 5×50 = 250. New sum = 5×52 = 260. Increase = 10. New boy = 45 + 10 = 55 kg.

questions.stem: The area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 10 cm is:

questions.stem: In a right triangle, sides are 5 cm, 12 cm, and 13 cm. The smallest angle is opposite to which side?

questions.stem: If sin θ = 3/5, find cos θ (assume θ in first quadrant).
questions.explanation: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. cos²θ = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25. cos θ = 4/5 (first quadrant, positive).

questions.stem: What is the author's primary message in the passage?
questions.passage_context: India's renewable-energy ambitions are unmatched in scale among major economies. The country aims to install 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel-based capacity by 2030, a target that, if achieved, will significantly alter the country's energy mix. Solar power has been the chief driver of this growth: prices have fallen by over 80% in the past decade, making it the cheapest source of new electricity in many states. Wind energy has played a complementary role, particularly in coastal states. However, the next phase faces structural challenges. Land acquisition, transmission infrastructure to evacuate power from remote sites, and end-of-life recycling of solar panels and wind turbines all require thoughtful planning. Storage — especially battery storage — is rapidly emerging as the most critical constraint, since renewable generation is intermittent. Without affordable storage, even ambitious capacity targets may not translate into reliable, round-the-clock clean power.
options: India should slow its renewable expansion
India's renewable target is achievable but faces structural challenges
India should focus on coal instead
Wind energy is no longer competitive
questions.explanation: The passage celebrates India's ambition but warns of structural challenges (land, transmission, storage).
questions.subject: ENGLISH
